page.layout: One page of text. Running head at the top left, page number at the top right. Italic verse block at full width at the top. Below it, a printed ornamental rule, then a centred heading in capitals with a subtitle. Then a paragraph of roman verse set beside a decorated initial. A signature mark at the foot, right of centre.

p.i: Pura. præsidium plebibus annuis Sed tandem vetitis luet Pœnas criminibus perdita debitas Quæ gens artificum manu Fictum numen amat, ritibus & colit Vanis. Quæ patris optimi Parere arbitrys dulcibus abnuit: Cuius larga benignitas Mortales variis muneribus beat. Huius magna vehām[?] sacer Vates perpetuis nomina laudibus. Tali vota Deo memor, Emersusq; nigris fluctibus offeram. Nam solus valido suos Servat magnifici robore brachii.

main_text.head: EX ULTIMO CAPITE Proverbiorum Solomonis, quo loco de veris matrisfami-liæ laudibus agitur.
main_text.p: FOELIX cui placido Numine contigit Consortem thalami ducere fœminam: Certo cuius amat fœdere castitas Servare incolumem coniugii fidem.

page.notes: The large initial F is a decorated woodcut letter, joined to "OELIX" in the printed word FOELIX. The ornamental rule above the heading and the printed signature mark are not text. Doubtful readings: "vehām" (the macron may be a printing mark) and the spelling "arbitrys" as printed. Spelling of u/v and i/j normalised in capitals and verse ("ULTIMO", "Proverbiorum", "Servat", "coniugii", "brachii").
